newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields end higher on softer crown.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields end higher on softer crown.

text.p: 1520 GMT - Swedish bond yields closed higher on Wednesday, stung by a weaker crown.

Lower than expected consumer prices for February did little to calm worries. CPI fell 0.1 percent in February from January, while market expectations pointed to an increase of 0.2 percent, according to a Reuter poll.

The crown was hurt by a report from a bank saying the Riksbank should raise rates to stop it from weakening further. * Six month T-bills climb three basis points to 4.30 pct * Ten year bond yields rise three basis points to 6.89 pct * Crown softens to 4.5090 to mark vs 4.4710 late on Tuesday

Yields ended higher and the crown weakened considerably on Wednesday despite publication of lower than expected February consumer prices. Dealers said that the market was entirely focused on the weakening crown.
The CPI decreased by 0.4 percent year on year and by 0.1 percent month on month. Expectations had been for a flat annualised figure and a 0.2 percent month on month rise.

Yields were pushed down by the weakness of the crown, which was further depressed by a Goldman Sachs report saying that there might be a need for a rate rise in Sweden in order to protect the currency.

The National Debt Office issued two billion crowns worth of nine year bonds at an average rate of 6.83 percent. Statistics Sweden released fourth quarter 1996 GDP figures but they were much as expected and had no impact on the market.
GDP rose by 1.8 percent between the fourth quarter 1996 and the same period in 1995, and by 1.1 percent between third and fourth quarter 1996.

The Six month T-bill rose three basis points to 4.30 percent and the 10-year bond yield rose three basis points to 6.89 percent. The crown fell to 4.5090 crowns to the mark from Tuesday's 4.4710. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
